A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CardioComposer. Their complete main texts and appendices, including rendered figures, tables, and equations, support reliable comparison despite the changed title, format, and expanded experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original cardiac-generation experiments, conditional-baseline comparisons, disentanglement and compositional-control evaluations, and biventricular biomechanical simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains original cardiac experiments and simulations and adds anatomical-system demonstrations, synthetic-ellipsoid experiments, and quantitative scaling, reconstruction, topology, and editing analyses.

M1.justification: The core latent-diffusion procedure and mass, centroid, and normalized-covariance guidance remain. Appendix 8.12 adds a bounded extension: separate extent and stretch MSE losses and a sign-invariant eigenvector-alignment loss for orientation. These enable finer control within the existing guidance framework. Boolean-union substructures were already demonstrated in v1.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained cardiac dataset, v2 evaluates separately trained models on branched aortic segmentations, CTSpine1K vertebrae, and ShapeMedKnee distal femur/cartilage segmentations (Sections 5.8 and 8.2). Appendix 8.9 also adds procedurally generated ellipsoids, substantially expanding anatomical and synthetic test coverage.

E2.justification: The principal comparators remain explicit concatenation with ANG, implicit concatenation with CFG, cross-attention with CFG, and the implicit component-dropout baseline. v2 additionally evaluates VAE reconstruction as a diagnostic reference against unconditional and guided generation in Appendix 8.10, Table 8.

E3.justification: v2 adds a training-fraction sweep with fixed validation data, a 24-case reconstruction/topology comparison introducing connected-component Betti error, a 64-case mass-editing sweep, and 32-sample alternative-loss evaluations. The ellipsoid experiment also changes model width and guidance weights. Separately, Appendix 8.4 revises the stated softmax temperature from 0.01 to 1; this establishes a reported setting change, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test dependence on training-set size, guidance behavior without anatomical complexity, reconstruction versus diffusion contributions to error, tolerance of extreme mass edits, and independent extent/stretch/orientation control (Appendices 8.8–8.12). The original component-loss and compositional analyses remain, although v1's numerical loss-ablation table is omitted.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The additional sample counts and 'seed label maps' in v2 describe experimental inputs, not repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial qualitative and numerical findings in Figures 12–14 and Tables 8, 9, and 11. For example, new Table 8 reports PA Betti error of 0.583 for unconditional versus 1.042 for guided generation. Retained compositional scores are unchanged, but v2 Table 1 omits v1 Table 2's two-component rows. v1 Table 1's numerical loss-ablation results are also omitted, while Figure 9 remains. New results should not be read as performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix 8.12 adds mathematical definitions for decomposing covariance into extent, normalized stretch, and orientation, with corresponding losses and a sign-invariant eigenvector-alignment formula (Equations 6–8). The original moment definitions remain equivalent. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of inference-time guidance without conditional retraining, independent attribute control, and compositional control persist. v2's abstract and conclusion add an explicit claim of demonstrated applicability across cardiac, vascular, and skeletal systems, extending v1's cardiovascular demonstrations.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies disentanglement through size–shape correlation and replaces v1's blanket inference that implicit models require retraining with an explanation based on dropout-configuration imbalance. It adds a limitation concerning within-class localized features, discusses transfer of guidance weights, and interprets topology and extreme-editing failures. Empty-segmentation instability remains documented in Appendix 8.4 despite leaving the main limitations section.

D1.justification: v2 supplies substantial additional reproducibility information: new datasets' label sets, case counts, resolutions and crops; ellipsoid-generation distributions; increased model width and adjusted guidance weights; and alternative-loss weights in Table 10. It also explicitly documents the EDM denoiser parameterization and revises the softmax-temperature specification. Core training hyperparameters and biomechanical-solver details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantive discussion of HUG-VAS and its fixed-connectivity restriction, adds A-SDF, EDM, and CTSpine1K citations, and trims several morphometry and statistical-shape references. The central positioning against conditional training remains. The anonymous ProtComposer reference becomes Stark et al.; this is the same cited work, not a new addition.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution statements, background, and much explanatory prose are rewritten. Terminology shifts toward 'substructures'; moment extraction and loss computation are consolidated, dataset and training sections are combined, and the appendix is reorganized and expanded. Algorithm 1 is removed, with its procedure retained in prose and Figure 2.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column layout with a predominantly single-column format and extensively rearranges, resizes, and recaptions displays. v1 Figures 5 and 6 move to appendix Figures 15 and 16. New Figures 12–14 and Tables 8–11 accompany the additions, while the original ablation table is removed and the compositional table is shortened.

improvement.justification: v1 acknowledges topology problems without quantifying them; v2 Table 8 distinguishes reconstruction, diffusion, and guidance errors, while Table 9 establishes degradation under extreme enlargement. These diagnostics, broader anatomical demonstrations, and more qualified baseline interpretation substantially improve understanding of applicability and failure conditions. The new anatomical demonstrations remain mainly qualitative, and omitted older result entries plus the unexplained temperature revision reduce traceability, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
